paragraphs.source_en: It’s easy to make fun of these legal theories, which is why we did so, but we hasten to note that we don’t think these advocates are stupid. More likely, these theories and similar ones are tactical—they are an attempt to shift the discourse. In 1967, whether a nation could take and keep Moon rocks was an open question. Five years later, two nations had done it and had not made a policy of sharing. Thus precedents are born. A purported loophole, repeated often enough that people in power come to believe it, might meaningfully shape the future, especially if it finds its way to the right politician or businessman.

paragraphs.source_en: This probably wasn’t technologically possible in either 1981 or 2012, even with vast spending. The least populous US state is Wyoming, with its six hundred thousand people.
